tast: Kill test bundles and related processes. Update test runners to create a new session for each bundle and kill all processes in the session (including processes started by tests) after the bundle exits. Also kill the session if the read end of stdout is closed while tests are running, as this typically indicates that the SSH connection was dropped. Otherwise, the processes can hang around forever. BUG=chromium:945626 TEST=added unit tests; also updated a test to launch child processes with both exec and testexec and checked that they're killed when "tast run" is interrupted Change-Id: I5e751ba828e21d0944a305d9a9eba64c16275095 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1543116 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

vm_tools: concierge: Run crosvm commands synchronously Currently concierge spawns a process to run a crosvm command but doesn't wait for it to exit. This is a problem at suspend time because concierge will report suspend readiness to powerd and the crosvm command process will race with the system going to suspend. If the system suspends before all vcpus have been stopped the guest kernel will panic on resume because it thinks there is a soft lockup. Always wait for the crosvm command process to complete before continuing. BUG=chromium:946847 TEST=suspend and resume a device with a VM running. check the logs to see that the "Setting resolv config" message appears in the logs after crosvm logs that the run mode has changed to running. Change-Id: Iba91729e126319c59f030d932003ffff3bd8e549 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1541848 Commit-Ready: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

vm_tools: concierge: Properly clean up child exits If crosvm exits on its own (for example, due to a guest kernel panic) then concierge doesn't delete the TerminaVm pointer correspending to that VM from the `termina_vms_` field in the Service class. This is a problem because the pointer is now pointing to freed memory and will cause a segfault if we try to dereference it later. Make sure to delete the TerminaVm pointer and also notify cicerone that the VM was stopped. CHROMIUM: config: denverton: Add timestamp support Add the CONFIG_NETWORK_PHY_TIMESTAMPING to the the Denverton splitconfig. Timestamping in the Ethernet PHY is supported in some server hardware Ethernet chipsets like those supported by Denverton, which is not widely available in other ChromeOS platforms. This provides the ability to do hardware-assisted LAN time synchronization for systems that are interested in this functionality. This change was generated from the following commands: cat <<EOF | tee -a \ chromeos/config/x86_64/chromeos-intel-denverton.flavour.config CONFIG_NETWORK_PHY_TIMESTAMPING=y EOF ./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig oldconfig BUG=b:127705522 TEST=CHROMEOS_KERNEL_SPLITCONFIG=chromeos-intel-denverton \ emerge-amd64-generic sys-kernel/chromeos-kernel-4_19 Change-Id: I7a44017b662966fa8f086558d5d6847d94fc13c6 Signed-off-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1544927 Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

If a device exceeds 16 collections (HID_DEFAULT_NUM_COLLECTIONS), the array to store the collections is reallocated, the pointer to the parent collection becomes invalid.
